desc:
A DNA string s uses only the letters A, C, G and T. A fragment is a substring of length exactly L.

Return the number of different fragments that occur at least twice in s. Occurrences may overlap.

s = "AAAAACCCCCAAAAACCCCCCAAAAAGGGTTT", L = 10
"AAAAACCCCC" occurs 2 times, "CCCCCAAAAA" occurs 2 times
result = 2
s = "AAAAAAAAAAAAA", L = 10
"AAAAAAAAAA" occurs 4 times (overlapping)
result = 1
constraints: s consists only of the letters A, C, G, T
hints: Collect all fragments of length L and count how often each one appears. What do you do with the ones that appear twice or more?
Storing each fragment as a string costs O(L) per window. Since there are only four letters, a fragment can be turned into a number.
Use 2 bits per letter and a rolling value: shift left by 2, add the new letter, and mask to the lowest 2 * L bits. A set of numbers records what has been seen; a second set records what repeated.
editorial: Map A, C, G, T to 0, 1, 2, 3. The fragment ending at position i is the number ((prev << 2) | code) & mask where mask = 22L - 1; the mask drops the letter that left the window. This gives a unique integer for every fragment (no collisions, because 2 bits per letter is a lossless encoding) and each window costs O(1).

Keep a set seen and a set repeated. If the current value was already seen, put it in repeated; otherwise add it to seen. The answer is the size of repeated. A fragment with three or more occurrences is still counted once because repeated is a set. Time O(n), space O(n).
